scope: 31 original-image-correct/subject-readout-wrong cases, plus31 unique successful controls. Same identity and scene preferred, foreground fraction nearest; matching is descriptive, not equal-view proof.
selection: All31 harms included, no score-based subset after intervention; control tie-break deterministic. Preserve the original full gallery and SHA ranking.
pixels: Decode original raw RGB without EXIF transpose, convert reviewed display-frame box back to raw. Keep size and processor grid. Far background excludes a two-merged-token-width guard outside subject. No resizing/cropping. Gray=127. Blur affects only far background. Matched background/subject masks use exactly the same pixel count, up to10percent of the subject interior, deterministic row-major blocks seeded per image; subject control is not presumed identity-free.
runtime: Pinned existing checkpoint, same inference runtime for every arm, unchanged reference cache. Original and lossless sham encoded independently; exact tensor equality required. Old-query parity and original full-gallery rank replay reported before interpreting interventions as old-error explanations.
matching: For fixed historical correct and center-error candidates, report independent MaxSim and baseline-argmax-locked matching, positive and negative absolute scores, and per-region contributions. No truth-based arm choice or weight fitting.
stages: Capture visual merger, final preprojection and retrieval embedding; compare corresponding token changes for pixel-unmodified subject tokens. Stage cosine is a sensitivity diagnostic, not a retrieval-trained head.
conclusions: Separate mask/readout boundary effect, encoded contextual dependence, and rematching/aggregation effects. Background-position usefulness is not background semantic identity. Pixel interventions may be out-of-distribution; two fills and same-count spatial controls are reported. No forced exclusive root label.
